fatal_errors: The proposed Co-Ni-Cr-B-Si/WC/B4C/TiB2 electrode is unrelated to the target mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders consolidated by SPS.
The hypothesis omits the central SPS-temperature intervention, its composition-specific temperature windows, and the comparison between three- and six-layer ESD coatings.
It claims wear resistance and effectiveness in aggressive environments, whereas the target study performed no wear, corrosion, or aggressive-environment performance testing.
The asserted fivefold wear reduction is not substantiated by the supplied evidence excerpts.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative ESD-coating hypothesis, and E1 directly supports the proposed electrode family, 25–35% binder range, coating dimensions, microhardness range, and qualitative adhesion/wear rationale. The controlled coated-versus-uncoated experiment could test the alternative hypothesis, although the aggressive environment and statistical design should be specified more precisely. It is not a reconstruction of the hidden study: it replaces the HEA compositions and SPS-to-electrode processing route with a different composite electrode system, omits the SPS temperature and layer-count comparisons, and predicts properties the target paper did not measure. Its baseline also misses the target's lower-temperature SPS and three-layer coating controls. Much of the intervention is closely derived from E1, so novelty is limited, while the quantitative fivefold wear claim exceeds the cited evidence.
